I've been with my wife for 5 years, own a house together, have an 11 month old daughter together, and couldn't be happier. We met on a dating site. Exchanged just a couple messages, said we should meet for drinks, we did, and really hit it off.

Online dating is great as long as you focus on the dating and actually meeting part. I had zero interest in talking online to anyone for long periods of time. I'd exchange 2 or 3 messages and try to set up a simple coffee or drinks date. Real life chemistry is everything, and people you are "meh" about online might really impress you in real life both in looks and personality. Granted, that can go the other way too lol. But people are a lot more than just a few pictures and a glorified resume. I spent one summer giving it a try and went on a lot of dates with girls I met online. The stigma of online dating is gone these days. There's plenty of beautiful, talented, and successful people on there.

So yeah, I had good experiences. I've met and dated women throughout my life in many ways. Through friends, from work, at the bar, etc. Online dating is just another way to meet people. Doesn't have to be the only way.

It's a great way to go on a lot of dates. A lot less effort than going to bars or whatever. Might be better for people older than mid-20s, since most younger folk are finding dates the old fashioned way.

Even though I think it's a good thing, I haven't been back on there since trying it out a few years ago. I still prefer to meet people in person through friends or work. Feels more right. But then again I'm single as fuck, so what do I know?
